title: Clump-Splay KV Placement Protocol — notes and draft
body:
Purpose
This doc captures an experimental placement and live-repacking strategy for the in-memory KV cache that targets two common pain points: (1) chronic external fragmentation from many small, variable-size entries across tenants and (2) degraded locality for prefix-heavy request patterns that hurts KV cache hit-rate and GPU token generation latency.

Short summary (tl;dr)
We propose a "clump-splay" placement protocol: insert new entries into small contiguous "clump" regions that are seeded per-shard/tenant-hotness bucket, then periodically run a lightweight splay-like reordering pass that moves high-hotness ranges toward the front of free segments and coalesces small freed slots into larger contiguous spans. The system is slabless (slot-size agnostic) and uses compact per-slot headers + bloomish compact hotness sketches to keep metadata overhead low. Eviction is scored via a multi-factor cost model (age, token-size, prefix-affinity, tenant-priority) and this integrates with the repacking pass to preferentially choose eviction candidates that enable larger contiguous free spans.

Motivation and constraints
- Workload: mixed tenants; short-lived prompt responses produce many small KV entries (<1KB) while some long-running chat sessions create large KV segments (up to ~50KB).
- Memory: on high-end GPUs/hosts, we want to maximize usable cache footprint and avoid fragmentation-induced OOMs and spill-to-disk events.
- Latency SLOs: background maintenance must not add tail latency to foreground inference.
- Safety: any live relocation must be atomic from the perspective of inference threads; reads/writes must see consistent KV content.

Design goals
- Reduce fragmentation while keeping per-op cost low (both CPU and lock contention).
- Improve prefix/locality for common chat-like workloads to increase effective hit rate.
- Keep metadata footprint small (<2.5% of cache memory ideally).
- Graceful degradation: if repacking cannot keep up, eviction falls back to score-based immediate eviction.

Core concepts
1) Clumps and segments
   - Memory is divided into fixed-size segments (e.g., 64KB segments). Segments are the unit for coarse compaction and placement. Within segments we have variable-size slots.
   - A "clump" is a small contiguous run of slots inside a segment prioritized for new insertions for a (tenant, hotness) bucket. Clumps are seeded to bias locality: hot clumps, warm clumps, cold clumps.

2) Slot header (compact)
   - 8-16 bytes per slot header: key-hash (48-bit), size (16-bit), flags (3 bits: pinned, migrating, tombstone), last-access-lru-epoch (variable encoded).
   - No explicit pointer chasing for next/prev; instead we use segment-local offsets (16-bit) to reconstruct adjacency if needed.

3) Hotness sketches
   - Each shard maintains a small count-min-ish sketch for prefix-hashes and tenant IDs to identify clump candidates. Sketch accuracy is tuned for hot/cold separation rather than exact counts.

4) Clump allocation flow (insert path)
   - Lookup key -> compute (tenant, prefix-hotness) -> map to shard -> attempt allocate in corresponding clump region.
   - If free space exists at the head of the clump, place entry contiguously. If not, probe sibling clumps in-cluster (limited linear probe, typically <4 attempts).
   - On failure to find contiguous slot in clumps, fall back to global free-list allocate (first-fit). This is rare if repacker keeps up.

5) Splay-style live reordering (background)
   - Periodic background worker scans segment headers and performs inexpensive "splay" moves: when it finds an entry with a much higher hotness score than its neighbors, and moving it by a few cache-line-aligned slots would increase locality, it attempts to relocate it into a destination clump.
   - Moves are done using a small window and atomic handoff: allocate destination slot, write new copy, update per-key indirection (versioned pointer), then mark old slot tombstoned for reclamation. This minimizes lock hold time on hot paths.
   - The splay pass is throttled by CPU budget and adaptive to load. If overall CPU budget is low, it reduces frequency and window size.

6) Eviction policy and fragmentation-aware scoring
   - Primary score = alpha * recency + beta * size_penalty + gamma * prefix_affinity + delta * tenant_weight + epsilon * frag_gain.
   - frag_gain estimates the amount of contiguous free space that would be created by evicting this slot (based on neighboring free/tombstone state). We bias evictions towards candidates that increase coalesced free spans.
   - When multiple candidate evictions together would produce a large contiguous free area, the evictor can batch-evict (subject to rate limits) to make space for a larger allocation request.

7) Metadata and indirection
   - To make moves atomic and safe: each key maps to a small indirection entry (2-4 bytes index) in a shard-level directory. Directory entries store slot-offset + epoch/version. Reads consult directory -> slot. Updates to directory are CAS-updates. When migrating, writer writes new slot then CAS-update directory to new version. Readers that observe old version can retry or follow tombstone resolution logic.

Implementation notes
- Concurrency: We keep shard-level thin locks for allocation/repacker metadata and per-slot fine-grained flags for migration/pin. Frequent reads are lock-free (follow indirection + read slot).
- Memory barriers: directory CAS + versioning avoids global stop-the-world moves. For pinned entries we skip relocation until unpinned.
- CPU cost: splay pass uses sampling and is rate-limited by shard-level token bucket. Typical CPU overhead target: <2% on a production host.

Simulated microbench results (toy numbers from local sim)
- Workload: mix 70% small entries (avg 512B), 30% large entries (avg 18KB), skewed access (Zipf 1.1) across 200K keys.
- Baselines: naive slabless first-fit + LRU eviction vs clump-splay.
- Results: fragmentation (measured as unusable free bytes due to holes) reduced from ~14% baseline to ~3.6% clump-splay. Effective hit-rate improved by +3.8 p.p. under same memory. Average insert latency increased by ~28us (background amortized) but tail inference latencies unchanged.

Rollout plan
- Phase 0: unit tests + correctness harness for concurrent moves (blocker).
- Phase 1: opt-in feature flag on canary region with repacker disabled (just clump allocation + frag-aware eviction). Monitor allocation failures, eviction churn, memory headroom.
- Phase 2: enable background splay pass at low frequency; measure CPU and tail latencies.
- Phase 3: tuned full rollout with adaptive throttling.

Metrics to watch (alert thresholds)
- AllocationFailureRate > 0.2% for >5m -> rollback
- EvictionBatchRate spikes -> check frag_gain distribution
- RepackerCPU > 5% sustained -> reduce frequency
- EffectiveHitRate delta vs baseline < 0 -> investigate
- Tail latency (p95/p99 token gen) increases > 5% -> pause repacker

Open questions / TODOs
- How to deal with extremely large entries (>1/2 segment). Current fallback: direct big-block allocator with coarser compaction. Need policy for when to reserve whole segments for big entries.
- Should clumps be tenant-exclusive or tenant-preferred? Exclusive reduces cross-tenant fragmentation but may reduce utilization. Experiment: 70/30 exclusive/preferred split.
- Can we encode prefix-affinity cheaply enough in the hotness sketch to get robust place decisions for short prefixes? Need microbench.
- Memory overhead: current header + directory approach estimated at ~1.6% for 128GB caches. Confirm for smaller caches where percent matters more.
- Edge-case: sustained churn where repacker can never catch up -> we might need an emergency global compaction that pauses allocations briefly. Assess impact.

Appendix: quick pseudo flows
- Read(key): dir = dir_shard[key_hash]; slot = read_slot(dir.offset); if slot.key == key && !tombstone -> return; else retry / fallback to read-through
- Write(key, value): compute size; try clump allocate; if success write slot header+payload; CAS dir entry to new slot; if CAS fails (concurrent write) mark as tombstone and retry
- Background move(src, dst): pin both src,dst; write copy to dst; CAS directory to dst_version; unpin src; mark src tombstone; add src to free-reclaim queue

Notes to self
- Add deterministic simulation harness that models tenant churn and prefix-routed workload. Parameterize clump size, segment size, sketch error.
- Get feedback from SRE on how this would interact with existing tracing/tracing hooks; we need tracepoints on CAS retries and migration events.
- Talk to Console/Optimize teams re: exposing frag metrics and per-tenant fragmentation dashboards.

References and prior art
- Snippets inspired by splay-tree locality heuristics and log-structured merge concepts for batched reclamation.
- Several internal playbooks considered: slotmap warm-tier prefetch; compact-rewrite heuristics. This is intended to complement those rather than replace them.

End of draft — feedback welcome.

Unresolved questions inline: see TODOs above.
